finding.claim: GET /users returns the id and name of every user in whatever org the caller names. There is no authentication or check that the caller belongs to that org, so any client can enumerate any tenant's users (IDOR / broken access control). This assumes no auth middleware is mounted outside this file. Only db.js exists in the directory, and req.pg is set by code that isn't here.
finding.sink: req.pg.query("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1") with results returned via res.json(rows)

trace.note: Route registered with no auth or authorization middleware
req.query.org is used directly as the tenant filter, not derived from a session or identity
Rows are returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: SQL injection ruled out because the query is parameterized ($1). No session, token or org-membership check exists in this file. No app.use middleware is registered. The other routes were also checked. /file confines paths with path.resolve plus a startsWith(ROOT + sep) check, so traversal is blocked. /count uses execFile with fixed arguments, so there is no command injection.

verdict.guard_found: none (only the parameterized $1 query, which stops SQL injection but not access control; no app.use or auth middleware in db.js)
verdict.reason: db.js:8-10 registers GET /users with no auth middleware and queries `WHERE org = $1` using the caller-supplied req.query.org, so an anonymous client can list any org's users; it could only be refuted if auth were mounted outside db.js, and db.js is the only file here.

verdict_facts.guard_found: none (the query is parameterized at db.js:9, which blocks SQLi but not IDOR; no auth or org-membership check, and no app.use middleware)
verdict_facts.reason: db.js:9 filters users by the client-supplied req.query.org with no check against the caller's identity or org, and db.js:8 has no restricting middleware, so any HTTP client can list any org's users via db.js:10.
